trial_court: District Court at Chhindwara, Civil Suit No.167-A of 2004
case_name: Anil Kumar Jain vs Maya Jain
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 1985 and decided to obtain a decree of mutual divorce due to differences between them. They filed a joint petition for divorce under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court dismissed the petition after the respondent wife withdrew her consent.

legal_principles.principle: The consent given by the parties to the filing of a petition for mutual divorce must subsist till a decree is passed on the petition.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that the consent given by the parties to the filing of a petition for mutual divorce had to subsist till a decree was passed on the petition.
cited_cases: Smt. Sureshta Devi vs. Om Prakash, (1991) 2 SCC 25

legal_principles.principle: If either of the parties withdraws consent before passing of the final decree, the petition under Section 13-B would not survive and would have to be dismissed.
legal_principles.held: This Court held that in the event, either of the parties withdrew the consent before passing of the final decree, the petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act would not survive and would have to be dismissed.
cited_cases: Smt. Sureshta Devi vs. Om Prakash, (1991) 2 SCC 25

outcome.final_order: The Supreme Court set aside the order of the trial court and granted the decree of mutual divorce to the parties.
